items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: He'd go there every night when Juanita would go off to play at this club... Oh yeah. Well she would tell me to watch Fats.

ctx.x: Well he had his own little group and his wife was the pianist in the band. Never had any great musicians. It was him and her. That was the biggest part of the band. And then they would just pick up any musicians. Fats and Lady Yes got to be a real contrary fellow. Couldn't anybody get along with him. I imagine that's because he was getting sick. And a man gets in a place where he's sick all the time. He becomes irritable and can't get along with anyone. He had this disease, the Bryce disease. But I stayed with…

He'd go there every night when Juanita would go off to play at this club. He'd go there and sit on the outside to keep Fats company. And Fats was on the last thing. Because he needed to see him alone.

Oh yeah. Well she would tell me to watch Fats. You know, I'd call her and she says, Come on over, I'm going to work. So I'd get over there and all the doors are locked. And so I'd go to the window and I'd eat that. I could raise his head up and tell him my cousin. I said, I don't worry about nothing. I said, if you get to the place where you really need me, I'm breaking the window. I said, well I need him locked all the house. When I'd come back she'd be all surprised. Thought she had left everything and all…
